### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **47** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**50** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 02ed8408450291fd22777fe9ba51a9ec9fcc9135`.

⛔ **17** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 49 pages)`
- **13** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **188** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 02ed8408450291fd22777fe9ba51a9ec9fcc9135` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `59cb1d10ce35f69d5a4b17de0e7802972156f5d2` — the merge of head `d2a38064eaaf69041dfa336855c26866c6f88c38` into base `02ed8408450291fd22777fe9ba51a9ec9fcc9135`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 59cb1d10ce35f69d5a4b17de0e7802972156f5d2 && git checkout 59cb1d10ce35f69d5a4b17de0e7802972156f5d2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 02ed8408450291fd22777fe9ba51a9ec9fcc9135 d2a38064eaaf69041dfa336855c26866c6f88c38 && git checkout -B drift-repro 02ed8408450291fd22777fe9ba51a9ec9fcc9135 && git merge --no-ff d2a38064eaaf69041dfa336855c26866c6f88c38

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 02ed8408450291fd22777fe9ba51a9ec9fcc9135
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 02ed8408450291fd22777fe9ba51a9ec9fcc9135` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Face: the file list (31 paths) holds one published-schema path (the ADR-0087 entry, first on the Scope line), and the PR body and the changeset both declare `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. The floor is every path of the diff outside the prose faces, 26 files. Inputs: card #35143, the claim 7206244272, the report 7209661255, the PR body, the net diff against merge base `ce4d8c7d7486fa5ab1fe4f33066a273c59a6b9f7`, the precedent records 7190867118 and 7194461560 for form, and the check-runs on this head. Everything below was read in the tree at this head; nothing was built or run.

The PR's three lines are called line 1 (seed keys), line 2 (object bindings) and line 3 (write grant) here, so that they are not confused with the finding ids.

### ① Derived judgments

- Line 1, `seed-record-unknown-field` (error; CLI and the `seed` door): RIGHT for a declared-field miss, with one remainder (S2).
  - The seed loader hands each record to the engine's insert with its keys as authored (`seed-loader.ts` strips only roll-up fields), and the engine's declared-field door refuses an undeclared key per row (`undeclaredWriteFieldErrors`, `engine-top-level.ts:2201`), so the row is culled in partial mode. The rule's set is the served field map plus `injectedColumnsFor`, which is `resolveInjectedSystemColumns`, the plan the registry's own injection reads. `id`, the tenant column, the audit family, the owner tier, `queue` and the sync columns are in it by the object's own flags.
  - Lookup keys are the field's own name, so there is no `_id` form to refuse. The loader gives no translation or companion key a pass the engine does not give.
  - Package-extended fields: counted on the CLI through `objectsAsServed` (the stack's extensions folded) and at the door through the served objects plus the batch's pending extension drafts (`runtime-authoring-gate.ts`, `foldPendingObjectExtensions`). Pinned.
  - CLI and door run one registry entry over one function. The universes differ as they must: the stack on the CLI; the served objects, the batch's drafts and, under `?package=`, the closure at the door. A dataset whose object the universe does not hold is not judged at either, so a draft object published alone, or an object outside the closure, yields no finding here.
  - Parity with `defineSeed` (`assertSeedKeysDeclared`, `seed.zod.ts:601`) is exact on the set. The engine's set is wider by two names: see S2.
- Line 2, `object-reference-unknown` at three more bindings: RIGHT at the runtime door; WRONG on the CLI for the flow-node site (M1).
  - Seed `object`, CLI only: adds a finding only for a platform-prefixed miss (a warning), since `defineStack` already refuses the unprefixed miss. Leaving the `seed` door to the #34864 refusal is right: that door accepts a draft of the object in the same package, and a served-object snapshot would contradict it.
  - Standalone action `objectName`: on the CLI `defineStack` already refuses the miss with the same two exemptions (`stack.zod.ts:6729-6738`: extended, known platform name), so nothing new is refused there. At the `action` door it is new and right: the pin it replaces recorded an action registered against no object and listed nowhere.
  - Flow CRUD and object-form screen nodes: the executors take `config.objectName` as written (`crud-nodes.ts:681`, `:773`, `:945`). At the door the universe is the served collection or the stated closure, and a miss there is a step that fails every run. On the CLI the universe is one stack, and that is M1.
  - The `noUniverse` guard and the `extended` exemption apply to the three new sites only. No existing site moved.
  - The `action` door now also runs the member's param `reference` / `objectOverride` check. Declared in the changeset. Right.
  - Drafts are not gated (`runtime-authoring-gate.ts`, D1), and a batch publish folds the batch's pending objects into the universe, so an object and the action or flow bound to it publish together.
- Line 3, `action-body-write-capability-undeclared` (error; CLI, `action` and `object` doors): RIGHT against the sandbox.
  - The runner passes `body.capabilities ?? []` (`quickjs-runner.ts:143`) and installs the six leaves behind `api.write` (`:754-756`); a denied call throws at the call site. The rule's list equals the runner's `WRITE`, and the pin reads the runner's source, with that file declared as a lint test input in `turbo.json` and `cross-package-test-inputs.mjs`. They cannot drift without a red.
  - Only `type: 'script'`, `language: 'js'` bodies are read, the set the runtime binds.
  - What the CLI lowers into that shape is S1.
- The extractor change (`extract-hook-body.ts:519`): RIGHT. `update\b` and `delete\b` could not match inside `updateMany` / `deleteMany`. The only build output that changes is `api.write` added to the `capabilities` of a lowered hook, action or job body whose only write was one of the two. No other reader in `packages/` keys on that token; the sandbox checks a grant only at a call.
- Public surface: no new export. `packages/lint` exports `.`, `./runtime` and `./rule-explanations`; neither `index.ts` nor `runtime.ts` is in the diff, and the new symbols and the added `ActionBodySite.capabilities` are module-internal. `./rule-explanations` changes text only.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`: RIGHT. Publishes that were accepted are refused, nothing an author can write is added, no export is added.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/lint` minor, `@objectstack/spec` patch, `@objectstack/cli` patch. One moved package at minor discharges `narrowed`, as in PR #37513 and #36691. The cli entry is a bug fix. No `major`.
- The changeset carries both declaration lines, the BREAKING banner, a FROM and TO section with three pairs, and the marker `adr-0087: registered publish-refuses-seeds-and-actions-that-save-and-do-not-work`, which is the entry's `id`.
- The entry is well formed (notice only, no conversion). Two of its sentences, and the same two in the changeset, are too wide: "a flow step bound to one fails the run on every execution" (M1) and "the seed load refuses a record with a key its object does not have" (S2).
- `packages/metadata-protocol`, `packages/objectql`, `packages/runtime` and `packages/qa/dogfood` are touched by test files only. No entry is owed for them.
- `Skills-docs: follow-up owed`: present and true. `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md:15-16` teaches the grant as prose ("without it the sandbox throws on a write"). The card is to be filed and the line rewritten to its number before ACCEPT; that is L1's item on a prose face.
- Check Changeset is success on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question in report 7209661255 (closure judgment on the `action` door): A, keep it.
  - ADR-0141 D1: "A dependency opens the reference", an undeclared cross-app reference is refused at the save door with 422, "the fix it prints is the declaration", and no second reference mechanism. B would make an action the one binding exempt from that.
  - The paired customization package declares its base (`protocol-customization-package.ts:501`), so the Studio customize route publishes an action on a base object as before. A package-less save is judged against the whole served collection.
  - What is refused under A: an authored package with no declaration that adds an action (or an action param reference) to another package's object. That is D1's rule, and the hint is the closure prescription. A stored action of that shape keeps running and is refused at its next publish, as the changeset says.
- Severity divergence the dev noted (flow node an error, flow trigger a warning): not accepted on the CLI. It is M1. At the door it is consistent, since the trigger is also an error under a closure.
- Hook bodies, `ctx.api.transaction` without `api.transaction`, the other tokens: not this family's lines. Cards for the seat.
- `updateById` in lint's `API_WRITE_METHODS` and in the `action-record-write-discarded` hint, with no such leaf in the runner's `WRITE`: outside this diff, the seat's to measure and file. The new rule's own list is the pinned one.
- Claim surface: the claim names `packages/lint/**`, the gate wiring, docs and one changeset. The diff also holds `packages/cli` (two files), the spec entry, `turbo.json`, `scripts/cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` and eight test files in four other packages. The PR body lists them commit by commit. The seat's scope line has to admit them, as 7190889569 did on #37513.
- Fixtures, each read:
  - Seven serve what the new rule asks for and change no assertion: the two `metadata-protocol` stubs and the three `objectql` conformance hosts now serve the object their flows and actions bind; the dogfood and the `runtime` uninstall fixture declare the package whose object the authored package binds. The subject of each test is untouched.
  - The eighth, `bound-action-foreign-object.test.ts`, is the one whose FROM moves: the orphan save was 200 and is now 422. Its assertions got stricter (code, status, issue rule and path, nothing registered) and the two that held before still hold. No pin was weakened.
  - `runtime-gate.inert-type-writes.test.ts` re-pins a fence from "an action write never reaches the suite" to "it reaches one member". The fence's reason (no parser at the door) is still enforced by the member filter and by the spawned-child probe added to `runtime-lazy-deps.test.ts`.
- `Security-touching: yes` is meant in one sense only: the rule's hint, the entry, the changeset and the docs row teach when a body must be granted the `api.write` sandbox capability, and the remedy raises a body's grant. The diff changes no enforcement, no permission check and no credential path. Whether that earns the `security` label is the seat's call.
- SQL push-down: the diff reads no data and adds no query. Nothing to report.
- Main is at `44ccf94a`; the head merges with it without conflict (merge-tree, no checkout). Main touched `authoring-rules.ts` and `validating-metadata.mdx` since the merge base and still registers 81 rules, the head 83.
- Check-runs on this head, read at 2026-11-27T04:29:03Z: 67 runs, 27 success, 9 skipped, 31 in progress, none failed, cancelled or timed out. In progress: Build Core, Test Core 1 to 10, Test UI 1 to 16, Build & E2E UI, Type Check UI, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates. Success includes Check Changeset, Dogfood Regression Gate, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, the Lint families, Type Check · source gates and · debt ledger, Build Docs. There is no red to give a cause for; the test and build families had not answered, so "all green" is not established on this head.

### ④ Design judgment

Against card #35143, Seeds and actions family only.

M1 (must-fix) — on the CLI the flow-node site refuses a binding to a declared dependency's object, which a build cannot see and the published contract says is not refused there.
- `validate-object-references.ts:604-610`: with no closure (the CLI never states one) and at least one own object, a `get_record` / `create_record` / `update_record` / `delete_record` / `screen` node whose `config.objectName` is an unprefixed name the stack does not carry lands on rung ② (`:315`), an error that fails `os validate`, `os lint` and `os build`.
- The same package's own rule on the same question hedges, on purpose: `validate-flow-trigger-readiness.ts:149-155` ("may be defined by another installed package, and this rule cannot see that package's objects. The hedge is real"), its explanation in `rule-explanations.ts` ("can be ignored when such a package declares the object"), and its hint ("or ignore this if another installed package declares it"). A flow in a dependent app now gets that advice on its start node and a build failure on the step next to it, for one object.
- Published: `content/docs/deployment/app-dependencies.mdx:174-179`, "Build-time validation cannot see a dependency's objects ... a binding to one is neither admitted nor refused there. The runtime save door is where a cross-app reference is judged". `validating-metadata.mdx` says the CLI doors skip such a binding "because there it may be a dependency package's object". ADR-0141 D1 puts the judgment at the save door.
- The diff's own comment grants the case: `:601-602`, "an app that declares none binds objects its dependencies own". So a stack with no objects is not judged and a stack with one object is refused for the same binding.
- The hint on the CLI ("Point it at one of this stack's objects, or at a platform object by its full name") names no fix for it. The only way through is an `objectExtensions` entry on the object.
- For that stack the changeset's and the entry's "fails the run on every execution" is false: with the dependency installed the step runs.
- The seed and action sites do not add this on the CLI (`defineStack` refused both before). The door is right as written. No pin covers a stack that declares a dependency it does not carry.
- Closing condition: with no closure stated, a flow node bound to an unprefixed object the stack does not carry does not fail the build (the trigger rule's split, advisory with no closure and an error under one, or an equivalent that reads the manifest's `dependencies`); a pin for that stack on the CLI beside the existing door pins; the changeset, the entry and the explanation say what is then true.

S1 (should-fix) — `os build` still lowers a handler into the shape line 3 refuses, and the hint does not apply to a handler.
- The CLI lowers before it lints (`compile.ts:392` then `:678`; `validate.ts:446` then `:719`; `lint.ts:814` then `:820`), and a lowered action body carries the inferred capabilities alone (`lower-callables.ts:572`). At run time the body wins over the bundled function (`app-artifact-handlers.ts:2076`).
- The extractor's write pattern needs the leaf directly after `.object(...)` and an argument with no `)` in it (`extract-hook-body.ts:519`). It infers no `api.write` for three shapes the new rule reads: a bound handle (`const repo = ctx.api.object('x'); await repo.update(...)`, the shape the extractor's own #16249 test treats as ordinary), `?.` before the leaf, and an object argument that contains a call.
- For each, `os build` now fails on a `target` function whose source is correct, with "Add 'api.write' to the action's body.capabilities", a key a function-valued `target` does not have. Before, the same handler built and answered 403 at every call, so this is the old defect surfacing at build, not working authoring refused. That is why it is not a must-fix.
- The rule's header says "a body `os build` lowers from a handler gets the grant inferred from its calls" (`validate-action-body-capabilities.ts:20-21`), which is untrue for those three. The dev closed the same class for `updateMany` / `deleteMany` and stopped there.
- Closing condition: the extractor infers `api.write` for every shape `bodyApiWriteCalls` reads, pinned shape by shape; or the finding on a lowered body names the handler-side fix and the header sentence is corrected.

S2 (should-fix) — line 1 refuses `created_at` / `updated_at` on an object that opts out of the audit columns, and gives a reason the engine does not bear out.
- The engine's door tolerates `id`, `created_at` and `updated_at` on every object, declared or not (`PLATFORM_PROVISIONED_COLUMNS`, `declared-read-columns.ts:82`, added at `:98`; the insert door's own note says the wildcard audit stamp relies on it). The seed loader does not touch the two keys.
- The rule's set is `injectedColumnsFor` (`validate-seed-record-keys.ts:68`), which drops the audit family under `systemFields: false`, `systemFields.audit: false` and `managedBy: 'better-auth'`. A plain `data[]` seed, or a `seed` saved at the door, that writes `created_at` on such an object is refused with "the seed load refuses this record ... and drops it". By the cited code the record is not dropped.
- The same sentence is published in the changeset and in the entry's `reason`. The pin "refuses an injected column the object opts out of, as defineSeed does" fixes the behaviour without asking the engine.
- Parity with `defineSeed` is a fair design, and `defineSeed` refuses the key for its own reason. The defect is that this rule's stated reason is the engine's refusal, and for these two names there is none. Read, not run.
- Closing condition: the rule admits the engine's provisioned names, or it keeps the refusal and the message, the changeset and the entry give the reason that is true for them.

Is a regex the right instrument for line 3 at a publish gate: yes, as an error.
- A false refusal needs a whole `ctx.api.object(...).LEAF(` spelled in text the mask exposes, or a shadowed alias (N1), and the named remedy clears it every time at the cost of a grant the body does not use.
- A miss leaves the author where main leaves every author today.
- The write list is pinned to the runner.
- A parser is barred at the door by the tier-1 fence, and a parser on the CLI alone would make the two doors disagree about one body.
- An advisory would let the publish through to a body that fails at every call, which is the card's complaint.

Nits, none with an effect on correctness or the contract:
- N1. The mask has two remainders the header does not list beside the regex literal: a nested template literal inside `${ }` (the inner text is read as code) and a regex literal that holds a quote (the rest of the line is read inverted). A parameter that shadows a bound alias is not counted by `boundOnce`. Each needs a whole write call spelled in the exposed text.
- N2. The two new ids have no `os explain` entry; the sibling `action-body-does-not-compile` has one.
- N3. ADR-0141 D1 and `app-dependencies.mdx` list the bindings the save door judges against the closure (a flow trigger, a dataset base, a list view). An action's `objectName` and a flow node now join them. The ADR note is Tier H: a card.
- N4. The re-pinned fence in `runtime-gate.inert-type-writes.test.ts` spells the member filter and its `['flow']` default a second time instead of asking the suite's dispatch.
- N5. `ActionSchema.objectName` admits the literal `global`, the object-less key (`action-governance.ts:76-84`). Written out, it is now refused at the `action` door as an unknown object, as `defineStack` already refuses it on the CLI. No producer in `ui/`, `packages/` or `examples/` writes it.
- N6. The flow-node list reads `config.objectName` on five node types. Other node types and the legacy `config.object` spelling are not read. A miss, never a false finding.

Open at this head: M1, S1, S2. Each earns a delta read of its fix by this reviewer.
